title: AbbVie (ABBV) Stock May Be 45% Below Fair Value As Rinvoq Expands In Europe - simplywall.st
content:
AbbVie stock has delivered a strong 153.8% return over the past 5 years, yet the valuation signals are split, with a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) intrinsic value suggesting meaningful upside while market multiples point to a richer price tag. For investors, the question is how to weigh that gap against the steady share price progress and recent product news around Rinvoq, Ubrelvy and the Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. The issue now is whether the DCF based intrinsic value or the richer market multiples offer the better guide to where AbbVie belongs at its recent US$246.04 share price. Find out why AbbVie's 28.1% return over the last year is lagging behind its peers. The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model values AbbVie by projecting future free cash flows and discounting them back to today. On this view, AbbVie’s latest twelve month free cash flow sits at about $18.3b, with analysts and internal estimates assuming growing cash flows over time rather than a sharp drop off. That stream of cash is what feeds into the 2 Stage Free Cash Flow to Equity approach used here. Based on those projections, the DCF model points to an intrinsic value of about $444 per share compared with the recent $246.04 share price. On this measure, the stock is described as 44.5% undervalued. The lowered full year profit forecast after the planned Apogee Therapeutics acquisition helps explain why the market is not giving AbbVie full credit for those cash flows right now. On the DCF math alone, AbbVie appears undervalued relative to its current share price. Our Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) analysis suggests AbbVie is undervalued by 44.5%. Head to the Valuation section of our Company Report for more details on how we arrive at this Fair Value for AbbVie. P/E works well for AbbVie because earnings are still a key anchor for how investors think about the stock. Right now AbbVie trades at about 69.3x earnings, which is higher than the biotech industry average of 17.3x and also above the peer group average of 27.2x. The fair P/E ratio implied by its profile is 39.7x. That is still well below where AbbVie trades today, even after the share price reaction to the updated profit guidance linked to the planned Apogee Therapeutics acquisition. The gap between the current 69.3x multiple and the 39.7x fair level suggests investors are paying a clear premium for AbbVie stock compared with what this framework indicates. On the P/E yardstick alone, AbbVie stock appears overvalued relative to both its sector and the modelled fair multiple. They spell out which future paths for AbbVie's growth, margins and earnings would line up with a much higher or lower stock price than today, and how those paths differ. Where a single ratio or model gives one number, these narratives describe the future that number depends on so you can watch over time whether that story is actually playing out. You can be one of the first voices in the Simply Wall St community to set out a number driven narrative on AbbVie and discuss where its cash flows, margins and execution could go from here. Share a view on how recent developments such as Rinvoq's expanded approvals or the planned Apogee Therapeutics acquisition might shape AbbVie's story, and then track how that thesis holds up as new results come through. Do you think there's more to the story for AbbVie? Head over to our Community to see what others are saying! For AbbVie, the Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) view points to meaningful intrinsic value upside, while the P/E comparison signals an overvalued stock on earnings-based measures. The broader set of valuation checks is weak, so that DCF signal sits against a backdrop where price and balance sheet metrics do not screen as cheap. The gap between the two views largely comes down to how confidently you treat AbbVie’s future cash flow path versus current market expectations for growth and execution. title: AbbVie (ABBV) Skyrizi Reclaims Top Spot In July Pharma TV Ad Spending Rankings - londoninsider.co.uk
content: AbbVie (ABBV) has reclaimed the number one position in pharmaceutical TV advertising after rival Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) briefly overtook it in June’s rankings. Skyrizi’s return to the top was driven by a $6 million increase in spending compared to the previous month, according to data from iSpot.TV shared with Fierce Pharma Marketing. Johnson & Johnson’s immunology drug Tremfya, which had briefly held the top position, fell to second place in July with $27 million in spending. That represented a notable decline for Tremfya, which had commanded $36.6 million in TV advertising spend just one month earlier in June. Johnson & Johnson’s atypical antipsychotic drug Caplyta made a strong move in July, rising two places to claim third position in the rankings. J&J increased its Caplyta spending by $10 million in July to reach $24.6 million, narrowly edging out AbbVie’s Rinvoq by just $1.1 million. Rinvoq, AbbVie’s second major immunology blockbuster, settled into fourth place after climbing from that same position in prior months of competition. Eli Lilly’s (LLY) popular obesity drug Zepbound slipped two spots to sixth place in the July rankings, representing one of the more notable movers in the period. A significant new entrant emerged in seventh place, with Johnson & Johnson launching the very first TV campaign for its oral plaque psoriasis drug Icotyde, which was approved in April. J&J spent $11.4 million on Icotyde’s debut TV campaign in July, signalling an aggressive push to build awareness for the newly launched treatment targeting moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. AbbVie’s Botox held eighth position despite a slight month-on-month decline, with spending falling from $13.4 million in June to $11.3 million in July. Lundbeck and Otsuka’s neurology drug dropped three positions to land in ninth place, reflecting a broader reshuffling across the mid-tier of the monthly rankings. Sanofi and Regeneron’s immunology drug rounded out the top ten, completing a list dominated by treatments for inflammation, obesity, and neurological conditions. The July data highlights how aggressively major pharmaceutical companies continue to invest in direct-to-consumer television advertising as competition intensifies across key therapeutic categories.
